server.instructions: Crow Memory — External synaptic memory for AI coding agents. Stores your coding style, bug intuition, and architectural preferences as compressed weight matrices in crow.bin.

crow_memory_bias.description: Auto-injected Crow Memory bias block. Contains your coding style, preferences, and evolved rules. The host should load this at session start.

crow_evolved_rules.description: Permanent evolved rules from Crow's system_prompt.md. These are statistically significant patterns approved via HITL.

crow_recall.description: Recall user-specific coding style, bug intuition, architectural preference, or personal context from the Crow synaptic memory. Call this BEFORE every response to align with user's inductive bias. By default (register=all or omitted, domain=all), queries all 8 registers and merges results globally by effective similarity.

parameters.query: Natural language description of the current task.
parameters.register: Which register. Use 'all' (or omit) to query every register in the selected domain. Code: style/bug/arch/context. Life: life_pref/life_avoid/life_phil/life_context.
parameters.domain: Domain filter used when register is 'all' or omitted. 'code' = style/bug/arch/context, 'life' = life_pref/life_avoid/life_phil/life_context, 'all' = all 8 registers (default).
parameters.format: Output format. 'hint' returns JSON hints (default); 'bias_block' returns the [User Bias] text block for system prompt injection.
parameters.project: Project tag used to boost same-project hints and filter/penalize cross-project ones.
parameters.strict_project: When true, hard-filters cross-project hints out of the results.

crow_ingest.description: Ingest a coding experience into Crow's long-term synaptic memory. Call AFTER build/test results or user explicit feedback. Provide either an explicit polarity or a build exit_code for automatic polarity mapping. Content is sanitized first; pure-noise input is rejected without touching the memory.

parameters.polarity: Reinforcement strength [-2.0, 2.0]. Optional if exit_code is given; explicit polarity wins when both are provided.
parameters.exit_code: Build exit code (0 = success). Maps automatically to polarity (+1.5/+0.5 on success, -0.5/-1.0 on failure) unless an explicit polarity is given.
parameters.user_edited: Whether the user edited the AI's output. Adjusts the exit_code-derived polarity.
parameters.project: Project tag stored with the memory entry for later project-aware recall.

crow_admin.description: Crow administrative operations in one tool. Actions: diagnostics (memory stats), drift (drift check), prompt (read/append/stats system_prompt.md), backup (create/rotate/list/recover), evolve (propose prompt mutations), project_info (list/create project instances).

parameters.action: Which admin operation: diagnostics, drift, prompt, backup, evolve, or project_info.
parameters.args: Action-specific arguments object passed through to the selected operation.

errors.project_name_required: project_name is required for create action

recall_messages.faint_bias: Crow recalls a faint {register} bias. Few memories stored yet.

evolve_messages.no_patterns: No statistically significant patterns detected yet.

drift_messages.confused: Crow memory seems confused. Recent tasks may be too novel or memory is saturated. Consider spectral reset or archiving.

> Do not edit manually — use the Crow MCP evolve tools.
system_prompt.managed_by: <!-- This file is managed by crow_mcp_server.py -->
default_rules: RULE: Before every response, call crow_recall(domain="all") to query all 8 registers (style, bug, arch, context, life_pref, life_avoid, life_phil, life_context) for the user's coding style, bug intuition, architectural preferences, personal taste, philosophy, and current context. Reflect the returned hints in your response.

RULE: After every response, ingest what the user revealed — preferences, philosophy, corrections, context — via crow_ingest. Judge the appropriate register and polarity yourself without waiting for the user to say "remember this." After code work, auto-evaluate build results via crow_ingest_from_build.
RULE: Do not skip the recall+ingest rules even for non-coding tasks such as document editing, git operations, or configuration changes. Always execute them.
